title: Water birds disperse seeds and eggs, explaining wide ranges of fresh-water life

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Water birds disperse seeds and eggs, explaining wide ranges of fresh-water life

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The wide distribution of fresh-water plants and lower fresh-water animals depends mainly on the transport of their seeds and eggs by animals, especially wide-flying fresh-water birds that move between often distant bodies of water.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: But the wide distribution of fresh-water plants and of the lower animals, whether retaining the same identical form or in some degree modified, I believe mainly depends on the wide dispersal of their seeds and eggs by animals, more especially by fresh-water birds, which have large powers of flight, and naturally travel from one to another and often distant piece of water.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter XII, “Geographical Distribution, continued”; section “Distribution of fresh-water productions”. Scope: fresh-water plants and small fresh-water invertebrates

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch12-03: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.65

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Movement, occurrence, and experimental data can demonstrate feasibility and test selected systems. They are less adequate for assigning a globally dominant causal share to waterbirds.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Link waterbird movement networks with viable seeds or invertebrate eggs recovered from plumage, feet, or digestive tracts and compare resulting connectivity with freshwater species genetic structure. Support requires bird-mediated routes to explain most long-distance colonization better than wind, water, or human transport.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Transport events are rare and seldom observed directly.

Distribution congruence does not identify the vector.

The claim that birds are the main cause requires quantitative data for rival vectors.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.77
discriminating power: 0.54
analysis feasibility: 0.59
operationalizability: 0.8
data adequacy: 0.52

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Bird movements and aquatic ranges are public, and some genetic studies line up with flyways, so a partial association test is possible. The causal ranking of birds over water, wind, and people is not in those databases. The mechanism can be examined for a handful of plants and microcrustaceans and not shown to be the main process worldwide.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Relate the genetic connectivity of widespread freshwater plants and small invertebrates to waterbird flyways, and compare documented bird transport of their seeds and eggs with transport by wind or water. Connectivity that follows bird movements more closely than other vectors would support the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Mainly requires a quantitative ranking of vectors that existing data rarely provide.

Transport experiments and vector comparisons are scattered in papers and are not one database.

People move aquatic organisms widely, which can create the same ranges.

data existence: 0.5

operationalizability: 0.6
